Hi Alex / MedWare security team —

Thanks for sharing the SOC 2 summary and completed questionnaire. A few focused asks so we can complete the qualification checklist on our side before procurement advances:

1) Pen-test report: can you provide a redacted PDF of your most recent external penetration test (redaction acceptable for PII/vuln specifics)? We’ll treat it as confidential. If you prefer, we can execute a short mutual NDA or provide a standard Redwood redaction checklist.

2) Vulnerability management SLAs: our security review typically requires target remediation windows we can rely on in the joint-risk assessment. Please confirm your expected SLA for severity tiers (Critical, High, Medium, Low) and whether you have a public disclosure policy. Our standard ask is: Critical — 14 days; High — 30 days; Medium — 90 days; Low — next cycle, but we can be flexible if you have statutory constraints.

3) Scanning cadence & tools: what automated scanning cadence do you run (weekly/biweekly/monthly) and which tools are used (Snyk, Nessus, Qualys, in‑house)? Do you perform external infrastructure scans as well as application tests?

4) Remediation verification: do you provide a re-test or attestations post-fix? If not, can we agree a timeline for verification after fixes are deployed?

If it helps, I can paste our standard vulnerability disclosure timeframe and the triage playbook during the call on Tue. Let us know whether the proposed remediation windows above are acceptable or what you typically commit to.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Karthik Iyer

Karthik / Grace —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a redacted copy of our latest external pentest (MedWare_pen_test_redacted_v1.pdf). Notes below summarizing our posture and answers to your questions: 

- Pen-test: External assessment performed 2026-11-12 by third-party (RedCrest Security). Report shared is redacted to remove CVE-level exploit details and internal IPs. We will execute an NDA if Redwood needs full technical artifacts.

- Vulnerability SLA: MedWare internal policy currently targets: Critical — 14 calendar days; High — 45 calendar days; Medium — 120 calendar days; Low — next release. For critical vulnerabilities that impact PHI flows we commit to emergency hotfix channels and will provide weekly status updates until closure.

- Scanning cadence & tooling: Internal pipeline runs Snyk (weekly) for dependencies, Qualys for external host scanning (monthly), and an internal scheduled dynamic scan (DAST) monthly. We run an external attack surface monitoring tool continuous‑feed for exposed credentials/hosts.

- Remediation verification: For High/Critical we provide re-tests by the original vendor or internal security team upon request; re-test lead times typically 7–21 days depending on complexity. We can provide attestations for fixes where re-testing is not feasible.

- Disclosure policy: We follow coordinated disclosure with a public advisory only after the vulnerability is mitigated or 90 days after report, whichever comes first, unless immediate public disclosure is required by law.

Let us know if MedWare's SLA windows are acceptable to Redwood; for procurement items we can also sign a 30/45/120 SLA schedule into the contract if needed.

Regards,
